findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff assumes SpansBuffer has an attribute `assigned_shards` and accepts a positional `shards` constructor argument (`SpansBuffer(shards)`), APIs that are not established anywhere in this diff or its context. If SpansBuffer's real constructor does not take shards positionally or `assigned_shards` does not exist, SpanFlusher.__init__ raises TypeError/AttributeError at consumer startup, taking down the process-spans consumer entirely; even if the attribute exists, each per-process buffer is constructed without any guarantee it polls only those shards, so processes may all read the same shard set and duplicate-flush segments to Kafka.

[BUG] When `produce_to_pipe` is set, a restarted flusher thread is never stopped: the `process.kill()` call is guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so the old thread keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement polling the same shards. After a 'hang' restart in thread mode (the mode used in both tests and any pipe-producer deployment), two threads concurrently flush the same Redis shard set, producing duplicate segment payloads to Kafka and racing on `process_healthy_since`/`backpressure_since` values; killed threads also accumulate for the lifetime of the consumer.

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` is defined but never called anywhere in the diff — dead code. A shard→process lookup helper with no callers misleads readers into thinking per-shard restart exists; the next person extending restart logic may wire it up expecting behavior (kill only one shard's work) the design does not support, since restarts always replace the whole multi-shard process.

[ADVISORY] Per-shard metric tags (`tags={"shard": shard}` and `"shard": shard_tag`) are emitted on high-frequency timers with unbounded cardinality as shard count grows. With shards-per-process across many flusher processes, `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `wait_produce`, `segment_size_bytes`, and `flusher_unhealthy` series multiply per shard per cause, inflating metrics backend cardinality and costs for operators who did not opt into per-shard telemetry.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten join() computes `remaining_time` and breaks without terminating remaining processes once the deadline is exhausted mid-loop, leaving later processes running after join returns. On shutdown with a timeout, processes after the one that consumed the deadline are neither joined nor terminated (the old code terminated its single process unconditionally), so spawned flusher processes can outlive the consumer shutdown sequence.

[ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts the internal shard count equals the partition count (4) without controlling how the buffer assigns shards, coupling the test to SpansBuffer's assignment behavior rather than the flusher's mapping logic. If shard assignment depends on consumer-group state or environment (e.g. fewer shards assigned in CI), `total_shards == 4` and `len(flusher.processes) == 2` fail for reasons unrelated to the feature, producing flaky CI; the test's real subject (round-robin mapping) is only checked via an aggregate count, so a mapping bug that drops a shard would not be caught if the count still summed to 4 via a different split.

[BUG] In join(), the `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the per-process loop entirely, so processes after the first timed-out one are never terminate()d, whereas the old code unconditionally terminated the single process. On shutdown with a timeout, leftover spawn-context flusher processes keep running inside the long-lived consumer after join returns, holding Redis connections and producing to Kafka after the strategy has been torn down.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code: no call site exists in this diff, and its lookup-and-restart logic is fully replaced by _ensure_processes_alive calling _create_process_for_shards directly. The next person touching restart logic has two near-identical paths to reason about; deleting the method removes a whole branch-mate with no behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The new --flusher-processes click option is declared here but no code in this diff reads the consumer's flusher_processes setting and passes it into ProcessSpansStrategyFactory, which defaults flusher_processes=None. Operators who set --flusher-processes on the command line get silently ignored values (the option parses and is dropped), so the flag ships inert unless wiring exists outside this diff.

[ADVISORY] The flusher now constructs fresh SpansBuffer instances per process instead of sharing the single buffer object it previously used, so any in-memory state on SpansBuffer (counters, queued segment data) diverges from the buffer instance the factory/consumer writes through. If SpansBuffer carries any non-Redis state, each process's buffer starts empty and segments written via the factory's buffer are never seen by the flusher processes; the diff silently assumes SpansBuffer is a pure Redis view and nothing verifies it.

[ADVISORY] The only behavioral assertion updated for multiprocess is the backpressure flag; the restarted-process path (no_process exitcode, hang detection, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError) and the join() timeout path are untested for the multi-process layout. A regression in _ensure_processes_alive's per-process restart bookkeeping (e.g. restart counter never incrementing, or killing the wrong process index) passes CI and only surfaces as a wedged span pipeline in production.

[ADVISORY] The new tags={"shard": shard_tag} on spans.buffer.flusher.produce / segment_size_bytes / wait_produce emits per-shard-group metric series whose cardinality scales with the number of shard groups per consumer. With many assigned shards the metrics backend accumulates one high-cardinality series per process grouping, inflating metric storage/cost with no aggregation or sampling guard added in this diff.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural invariants (process counts, shard-map sums) and never submits a segment or verifies a flush, so it does not verify that shards multiplexed onto a shared process actually get flushed and produced. A bug where a shared process only polls its first shard (or drops other shards' segments) passes this test; the end-to-end multiplexed-flush behavior added by this diff has no coverage.

[BUG] The rewritten join() breaks out of the outer process loop when the deadline expires, skipping terminate() for the remaining processes and leaving them running. During consumer shutdown with a timeout, after the first process exhausts the deadline the `break` exits the for-loop, so later processes are neither waited on nor terminated; spawned flusher processes outlive join() and keep producing to Kafka after the strategy has reported shutdown.

[BUG] Memory backpressure accounting now sums used/available across per-shard SpansBuffer instances that all point at the same Redis, so `available` is inflated by a factor of num_processes. With N shard buffers reporting the same Redis capacity, `used / available` is diluted N-fold and the `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` guard effectively trips at N times the configured threshold, reintroducing the unbounded Redis backlog the check exists to prevent.

[BUG] Default flusher behavior silently changes from one shared process to one process per shard whenever `flusher_processes` is not passed, with no default enforced at the factory. Any existing call site that constructs ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without the new parameter (other consumer configs, scripts, simulators) goes from 1 flusher process to len(assigned_shards) processes, multiplying Redis connections and spawn overhead per partition without anyone opting in.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds an unrelated hasattr-vs-isinstance coding guideline to CLAUDE.md with no connection to the span buffer multiprocess work. Unrelated expansion bundled into a span-consumer PR: reviewers of the flusher change must vet a docs convention change, and reverting or cherry-picking the flusher work drags the doc change along.

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code never called anywhere in the diff. A linear-scan helper that duplicates the shard-to-process mapping knowledge lingers as an unused branch; the next change to the mapping must reason about a code path that never executes.

[ADVISORY] Metric tag naming drifts: produce/segment_size use `shard` while wait_produce uses `shards` for the same cardinality-heavy shard-list value. Dashboards and alerts built on one tag name miss the other series, and the comma-joined shard-list tag creates unbounded tag combinations that inflate metrics cardinality per process grouping.

[ADVISORY] test_basic now relies on a real `time.sleep(0.1)` to wait for a spawn-mode flusher, introducing wall-clock flakiness while the very next line monkeypatched sleep away earlier in the same test. On slow or loaded CI the 100ms window is not enough for the spawned flusher to observe the drift change and flush, producing an intermittent empty-`messages` failure unrelated to product code.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only the shard-mapping bookkeeping (counts and dict sizes) and never exercises an actual flush through a shared process, so the core behavior — multiple shards flushed correctly by one process — is untested. A regression where a shared process flushes only the first shard in its list (e.g. an off-by-one in the buffer or the `shards` arg plumbing) passes this test while dropping spans for the remaining shards in production.

[BUG] _create_process_for_shards constructs fresh SpansBuffer(shards) instances instead of sharing the buffer instance the consumer's write path uses, so the buffer passed into SpanFlusher is now used only for len(buffer.assigned_shards) and every flusher-side buffer is a disconnected empty instance. Any SpansBuffer state that is instance-local rather than derived purely from Redis (segment bookkeeping consumed by record_stored_segments, memory accounting used by get_memory_info) exists separately in the writer's buffer and in each per-process buffer; record_stored_segments() in submit() now runs against instances nothing was ever written into, and a restart replaces the buffer again, silently resetting whatever counters/state it held. If any part of the flush path depends on buffer-instance state rather than a pure Redis read, segments are never flushed or are accounted incorrectly.

[BUG] self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) makes the factory default (flusher_processes=None) spawn one process per shard, while the new CLI option defaults to 1, so existing non-CLI constructions of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory silently change from 1 flusher process to N processes. Every caller that constructs ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without passing flusher_processes (other consumers, dev tooling, tests) multiprocesses the flusher without opting in, multiplying spawn-process count and Redis polling load by the shard count; additionally a configured flusher_processes=0 silently falls back to one-process-per-shard via the `or` instead of being rejected or clamped.

[ADVISORY] The two adjacent timers tag the same value under different tag names: metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag}) vs metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag}). Dashboards and alerts that group by one tag name silently miss the other metric's per-shard breakdown, and the newly tagged segment_size_bytes uses "shard" while wait_produce uses "shards", so per-shard latency comparison across the flush pipeline is impossible without a metric-name fix deploy.

[ADVISORY] The backpressure check now raises MessageRejected if ANY single process's backpressure_since is past the threshold, so one slow/hung shard process backpressures the entire consumer including shards assigned to healthy processes. With flusher_processes > 1, a single lagging shard (e.g., one hot org's segments) stalls ingestion for all partitions, whereas previously backpressure reflected the single shared flusher; operators see consumer-wide throughput drops traceable to one shard, and the multi-process parallelism this PR adds is negated whenever any one process falls behind.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — no call site exists in this diff; restarts route exclusively through _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards). The next reader must determine whether per-shard restart (and its interaction with the process_to_shards_map) is a supported path; the unused method implies an intended restart granularity that was never wired up, and it will silently rot if the mapping shape changes.

[ADVISORY] In join(), the `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the entire for-loop over processes, so once the deadline expires no remaining process gets the terminate() call that the old single-process code always executed. On a join timeout, all but the already-processed prefix of flusher processes are abandoned without terminate(); they survive as daemon processes until interpreter exit, and any shutdown path that relies on terminate() to unblock a stuck flusher (e.g., a hung Redis poll in main) now leaves N-1 processes spinning during the rest of shutdown.

[ADVISORY] Unhealthy detection now operates at process granularity but reports and restarts per shared process: a hang caused by one shard's data kills and restarts the process serving all its co-assigned shards, and the unhealthy metric is emitted once per shard with no way to attribute which shard caused it. Operators debugging flusher_unhealthy spikes see every shard in the group flagged simultaneously and cannot distinguish the offending shard; with the default round-robin assignment i % num_processes, a single pathological shard repeatedly crashes its co-tenant shards' flushing, and the shared process_restarts counter trips the consumer-restarting RuntimeError due to one shard's bad data.

[BUG] When a threaded flusher (produce_to_pipe path) is judged unhealthy with cause 'hang', the code restarts the process without terminating the old one, leaving two flusher threads polling the same shards. The old thread's loop continues until self.stopped is set (only at join), so both the old and new thread flush the same shards and produce duplicate span segment payloads to Kafka; downstream consumers see duplicated data. The old single-process code crashed loudly here (AttributeError on Thread.kill escaping the ValueError-only handler); the new code silently converts that crash into data duplication.

[BUG] The added 'give flusher threads time to process' time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op lambda two lines earlier. The synchronization step the test author added to fix a race does nothing, so test_basic still races between the flusher thread's polling loop and step.join(); the test remains flaky and the review iteration that 'fixed' the flakiness changed nothing, masking the real synchronization gap.

[ADVISORY] The docstring now claims 'Creates one process per shard' while the code implements round-robin shard grouping via process_to_shards_map, and the effective default (max_processes None -> len(buffer.assigned_shards)) diverges from the CLI default of 1. The stated intent in the artifact contradicts the implemented behavior; callers that construct ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without the new flag silently move from one flusher process to one-per-shard spawn processes (N× process count, N× Redis connections), a resource-usage change no human explicitly accepted since the user-facing default was pinned to 1.

[ADVISORY] test_basic was silently changed from @pytest.mark.django_db to @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True) without explanation, weakening test isolation to make the new multiprocess path pass. The test now runs against a non-transactional database, so any real bug in the multiprocess flush path that manifests as transaction interaction is hidden rather than caught; future failures in this test will be harder to attribute because the isolation change was made to accommodate the implementation rather than reviewed as a behavioral signal.

[ADVISORY] The new metric tags use inconsistent keys: 'shard' on spans.buffer.flusher.produce/segment_size_bytes but 'shards' on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce. Dashboards and alerts that group by shard tag will split wait_produce data into a separate tag dimension, producing silently fragmented metrics for operators monitoring the new per-shard health behavior this PR introduces.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten join() breaks out of the process loop when the deadline expires, skipping terminate() for all remaining processes, and never terminates threaded flushers at all. On shutdown timeout, some spawn processes are left running past the consumer's join deadline (previously the single process was always terminated), leaking spawn processes holding Redis connections during deploy restarts.

[ADVISORY] The multi-process restart and health-monitoring logic (_ensure_processes_alive, per-process restart counters, shard-group restarts) has no test coverage in this diff. A regression in the restart path — e.g. the duplicate-thread bug or the restart counter now incrementing per poll across a shared shard group — would ship silently, since both new tests only exercise the healthy happy path where no process dies or hangs.

[BUG] test_basic adds `time.sleep(0.1)` 'to give flusher threads time to process', but the test's first line monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), so the added sleep does nothing and the test still depends on a race between the flusher process and step.join(). The test is flaky in exactly the way the added lines claim to fix: if the flusher hasn't yet drained the segment when step.join()/step.poll() completes, messages is empty and `(msg,) = messages` raises IndexError; on faster machines it passes while never actually synchronizing, giving false confidence in the new multiprocess flush path.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only the flusher's internal bookkeeping (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, total_shards) and never submits any message or asserts any flushed payload, so it verifies the constructor's shard-mapping arithmetic, not parallel flushing behavior. A regression in the actual sharding logic — e.g. _create_process_for_shards restarting the wrong process, or a process flushing the wrong shards (the shard->process map is never exercised at runtime) — passes this test; only test_flusher.py's single-process backpressure assertion covers the flusher at all, so the core new behavior (multiple processes each flushing their own shards) has zero behavioral coverage in the diff (checked: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py and test_flusher.py are the only changed spec files).

[ADVISORY] The old assertion `flusher.backpressure_since.value` was replaced with `any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`, which passes when any single process is in backpressure even though the new submit() raises MessageRejected only per-process — the test no longer pins which process's backpressure triggered and would pass even if only one of N processes is stuck while the test's submit path depends on all of them. A bug in the new submit() loop (e.g. iterating only the first process's backpressure_since due to a dict mutation during restart) still satisfies this assertion, weakening the backpressure regression guard compared to the pre-diff test.

[ADVISORY] The reworked _ensure_processes_alive restart path — including the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) kill guard for thread-mode flushers, and _create_process_for_shards — is exercised by no test in the diff (checked: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py only asserts backpressure state; test_consumer.py only asserts process counts and a happy-path flush). A regression in the restart loop — e.g. self.process_restarts[process_index] incremented but _create_process_for_shards never replacing the dead entry, leaving self.processes holding a dead process forever — ships silently; the thread-mode (produce_to_pipe) branch where process.kill() is skipped is entirely untested.

[ADVISORY] Both tests were converted from @pytest.mark.django_db to @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True) with no comment or associated production change explaining why transactional DB access is now required. Transactional tests are slower and cannot use TestCase-level rollback isolation; if the conversion was needed because the spawn-based flusher processes access the DB outside the test transaction, that cross-process DB dependency is itself untested behavior that will behave differently in production (real spawned processes) than under the test runner.

[BUG] join()'s `break` on deadline exhaustion skips the terminate() (and any wait) for every remaining process, so on shutdown timeout only the first process is ever terminated. With multiple flusher processes, once the join deadline expires while waiting on the first process, the loop breaks and processes 2..N are never terminated or joined — orphaned spawn processes keep flushing Redis and producing to Kafka after the consumer has been torn down, duplicating work against whatever replacement consumer takes over the partitions. The old single-process code called terminate() unconditionally.

[ADVISORY] For threading.Thread flushers (produce_to_pipe path), a process diagnosed as 'hang' is never stopped — the isinstance guard skips kill() and a replacement thread is started for the same shards while the hung thread keeps running. Two threads concurrently poll and flush the same Redis shards, racing to produce the same segments to Kafka and fighting over Redis deletes — duplicate payloads and corrupted flush bookkeeping; the 'restarted' process is a lie because the old one is still alive. Anyone running the flusher with produce_to_pipe (tests, in-memory pipelines) gets silent duplicate work after any hang.

[ADVISORY] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit flusher_processes of 0 as 'unset', silently escalating it to one-process-per-shard. An operator who passes --flusher-processes 0 (or a config that computes 0) intending to disable parallelism/disable flushing gets the maximum fan-out instead; the falsy-zero makes the CLI default=1 option's semantics undocumented and unenforceable, and any negative value produces num_processes < 0 and zero flusher processes with no error.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — nothing in the diff or its call sites invokes it. Future maintainers get a misleadingly-named single-shard restart helper that silently restarts the whole shared process (it delegates to _create_process_for_shards), so a caller using it to restart one shard actually kills and recreates the process owning several shards, momentarily stopping flushes for unrelated shards.

[ADVISORY] Metric tag key drifts between 'shard' (produce timer, segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (wait_produce timer) for the same comma-joined shard list. Dashboards/alerts that group by shard tag silently miss the wait_produce series (or vice versa), so a hang in the produce-wait stage looks like a gap rather than a slow stage; also the comma-joined multi-shard tag value creates a distinct series per shard-grouping permutation, fragmenting the metric.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff assumes SpansBuffer has an attribute `assigned_shards` and accepts a positional `shards` constructor argument (`SpansBuffer(shards)`), APIs that are not established anywhere in this diff or its context. If SpansBuffer's real constructor does not take shards positionally or `assigned_shards` does not exist, SpanFlusher.__init__ raises TypeError/AttributeError at consumer startup, taking down the process-spans consumer entirely; even if the attribute exists, each per-process buffer is constructed without any guarantee it polls only those shards, so processes may all read the same shard set and duplicate-flush segments to Kafka.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `SpanFlusher.__init__` newly relies on `buffer.assigned_shards` (e.g., `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `for i, shard in enumerate(buffer.assigned_shards)`), and `_create_process_for_shards` constructs new buffers via `SpansBuffer(shards)`. The diff does not show `SpansBuffer`’s implementation or any accompanying change proving these APIs exist or are correct, so the finding’s “could raise TypeError/AttributeError at startup” is a concrete compatibility risk but not verifiable from the diff alone. Likewise, whether per-process buffers truly isolate shards depends on `SpansBuffer` internals not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When `produce_to_pipe` is set, a restarted flusher thread is never stopped: the `process.kill()` call is guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so the old thread keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement polling the same shards. After a 'hang' restart in thread mode (the mode used in both tests and any pipe-producer deployment), two threads concurrently flush the same Redis shard set, producing duplicate segment payloads to Kafka and racing on `process_healthy_since`/`backpressure_since` values; killed threads also accumulate for the lifetime of the consumer.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher is unhealthy it restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` but only attempts to stop the old worker with `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. In `produce_to_pipe` mode the worker is a `threading.Thread` (see `_create_process_for_shards`: `make_process = threading.Thread`), so the old thread is never terminated or signaled to stop during a restart (the shared `self.stopped` flag is only set in `join()`, not on restart). This means a hang-triggered restart can leave the old thread running while a replacement thread starts polling the same `shards`, with both threads sharing the same `process_healthy_since[...]`/`process_backpressure_since[...]` `mp_context.Value` objects passed into `main`, causing concurrent operation and potential duplicate flushing/metric races and leaking threads over the consumer lifetime.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly defined, but the diff shows no references/calls to it (restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` always calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Per-shard metric tags (`tags={"shard": shard}` and `"shard": shard_tag`) are emitted on high-frequency timers with unbounded cardinality as shard count grows. With shards-per-process across many flusher processes, `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `wait_produce`, `segment_size_bytes`, and `flusher_unhealthy` series multiply per shard per cause, inflating metrics backend cardinality and costs for operators who did not opt into per-shard telemetry.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds per-shard (or shard-list) metric tags on potentially frequent instrumentation points: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` inside the flusher loop, and `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})` for each shard on health failures. These changes can materially increase metrics cardinality proportional to shard count (and shard-combinations for `shard_tag`), which is an operational/cost concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten join() computes `remaining_time` and breaks without terminating remaining processes once the deadline is exhausted mid-loop, leaving later processes running after join returns. On shutdown with a timeout, processes after the one that consumed the deadline are neither joined nor terminated (the old code terminated its single process unconditionally), so spawned flusher processes can outlive the consumer shutdown sequence.

[ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts the internal shard count equals the partition count (4) without controlling how the buffer assigns shards, coupling the test to SpansBuffer's assignment behavior rather than the flusher's mapping logic. If shard assignment depends on consumer-group state or environment (e.g. fewer shards assigned in CI), `total_shards == 4` and `len(flusher.processes) == 2` fail for reasons unrelated to the feature, producing flaky CI; the test's real subject (round-robin mapping) is only checked via an aggregate count, so a mapping bug that drops a shard would not be caught if the count still summed to 4 via a different split.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the test explicitly constructs `partitions = {Partition(topic, i): 0 for i in range(4)}` and passes them to `fac.create_with_partitions(...)`, so from the diff shown the shard/partition count is under the test’s control rather than being derived from consumer-group/environment state. The new flusher mapping logic also deterministically iterates `for i, shard in enumerate(buffer.assigned_shards)` and appends each shard to exactly one bucket, so a “dropped shard but still sums to 4” scenario is not supported by the code shown (the sum reflects the input list length). Claims about CI assigning fewer shards or shard assignment depending on external state are not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In join(), the `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the per-process loop entirely, so processes after the first timed-out one are never terminate()d, whereas the old code unconditionally terminated the single process. On shutdown with a timeout, leftover spawn-context flusher processes keep running inside the long-lived consumer after join returns, holding Redis connections and producing to Kafka after the strategy has been torn down.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` computes `remaining_time` and does `if remaining_time <= 0: break`, which exits the *entire* per-process iteration. That means if the deadline has been exceeded while waiting on an earlier process, any later processes are never reached and thus never `terminate()`d (the `terminate()` call is inside the `for` body). In the prior single-process version, the sole process was always terminated after the wait loop. With multiple flusher processes now possible (`self.processes` dict), this can leave some alive after `join()` returns when `timeout` is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code: no call site exists in this diff, and its lookup-and-restart logic is fully replaced by _ensure_processes_alive calling _create_process_for_shards directly. Restart logic is handled via `_ensure_processes_alive()`, which directly calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` for unhealthy processes. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new Click option is added to the consumer config and that `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`/`SpanFlusher` now accept and use a `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` parameter. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The flusher now constructs fresh SpansBuffer instances per process instead of sharing the single buffer object it previously used, so any in-memory state on SpansBuffer (counters, queued segment data) diverges from the buffer instance the factory/consumer writes through. If SpansBuffer carries any non-Redis state, each process's buffer starts empty and segments written via the factory's buffer are never seen by the flusher processes; the diff silently assumes SpansBuffer is a pure Redis view and nothing verifies it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavioral assumption change: `SpanFlusher.__init__` no longer stores the passed `buffer` (`self.buffer = buffer` removed) and `_create_process_for_shards` now creates a fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process (`shard_buffer`) and uses those in `main()`, while `submit()` now calls `record_stored_segments()`/`get_memory_info()` on `self.buffers.values()` instead of the original buffer. If `SpansBuffer` has any in-memory state that is expected to be shared with the producer/writer side, this change could desync it; the diff does not verify/guarantee `SpansBuffer` is purely a Redis view. However, from the diff alone we can’t confirm `SpansBuffer` actually carries such non-Redis state, so it’s an architecture/assumption concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only behavioral assertion updated for multiprocess is the backpressure flag; the restarted-process path (no_process exitcode, hang detection, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError) and the join() timeout path are untested for the multi-process layout. A regression in _ensure_processes_alive's per-process restart bookkeeping (e.g. restart counter never incrementing, or killing the wrong process index) passes CI and only surfaces as a wedged span pipeline in production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff substantially refactors SpanFlusher from a single background process/thread to multiple per-shard (or shared) processes with new per-process state: `processes`, `process_to_shards_map`, `process_restarts` dict, `process_healthy_since`, and `_ensure_processes_alive()` restart/kill logic (including MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError) plus a new multi-process `join()` loop. The only test updates tied to this refactor are (a) `test_flusher` changing the backpressure assertion to `any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())` and (b) a new `test_flusher_processes_limit` that asserts process count/shard distribution. There are no tests exercising the new multi-process failure paths (dead process exitcode -> restart, hang detection via `process_healthy_since`, restart counter increments per index, killing the correct process, or join-timeout behavior). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for nontrivial new logic rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new tags={"shard": shard_tag} on spans.buffer.flusher.produce / segment_size_bytes / wait_produce emits per-shard-group metric series whose cardinality scales with the number of shard groups per consumer. With many assigned shards the metrics backend accumulates one high-cardinality series per process grouping, inflating metric storage/cost with no aggregation or sampling guard added in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds shard-group tags derived from a comma-joined list of shards (`shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))`) and uses them in metric calls: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, and `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. Since `shard_tag` varies with the shard grouping assigned to each flusher process, this can create additional metric series per distinct shard-group per consumer instance. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded operational/observability concern (cardinality/cost), not a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural invariants (process counts, shard-map sums) and never submits a segment or verifies a flush, so it does not verify that shards multiplexed onto a shared process actually get flushed and produced. A bug where a shared process only polls its first shard (or drops other shards' segments) passes this test; the end-to-end multiplexed-flush behavior added by this diff has no coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the test only checks `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, and that `process_to_shards_map` covers 4 shards, then calls `step.join()` without ever submitting any messages/segments or asserting anything was produced to `messages` (it passes `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` but never checks it). Given the diff adds nontrivial shard-to-process multiplexing in `SpanFlusher` (`process_to_shards_map`, per-process buffers, `SpanFlusher.main(..., shards=...)`), the test does not exercise or validate that all shards assigned to a shared process are actually polled/flushed/produced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten join() breaks out of the outer process loop when the deadline expires, skipping terminate() for the remaining processes and leaving them running. During consumer shutdown with a timeout, after the first process exhausts the deadline the `break` exits the for-loop, so later processes are neither waited on nor terminated; spawned flusher processes outlive join() and keep producing to Kafka after the strategy has reported shutdown.
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same core problem: the loop breaks when the deadline expires, which prevents terminate() from being called on remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Memory backpressure accounting now sums used/available across per-shard SpansBuffer instances that all point at the same Redis, so `available` is inflated by a factor of num_processes. With N shard buffers reporting the same Redis capacity, `used / available` is diluted N-fold and the `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` guard effectively trips at N times the configured threshold, reintroducing the unbounded Redis backlog the check exists to prevent.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the memory backpressure check changed from `memory_infos = list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())` to iterating over `self.buffers.values()` and summing `used`/`available` across all per-process `SpansBuffer` instances (created as `SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`). If those buffers report `ServiceMemory` for the same underlying Redis service (likely, since only shards differ), then `available` (and `used`) will be double-counted per buffer, diluting `used/available` by roughly the number of buffers and weakening the `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` guard. The diff directly introduces this summation across multiple buffers without any de-duplication by service identity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Default flusher behavior silently changes from one shared process to one process per shard whenever `flusher_processes` is not passed, with no default enforced at the factory. Any existing call site that constructs ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without the new parameter (other consumer configs, scripts, simulators) goes from 1 flusher process to len(assigned_shards) processes, multiplying Redis connections and spawn overhead per partition without anyone opting in.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the default when `max_processes` is `None` is `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, which results in `num_processes == len(assigned_shards)` (one process per shard) whenever the new parameter is not provided. `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` sets `flusher_processes: int | None = None` and passes `max_processes=self.flusher_processes`, so any existing call site that doesn’t pass the new arg will now spawn per-shard processes instead of the previous single process (`_create_process()` in the old code). Only the CLI path adds a click option defaulting to 1; the factory itself does not enforce that default. This is a silent default behavior change verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds an unrelated hasattr-vs-isinstance coding guideline to CLAUDE.md with no connection to the span buffer multiprocess work. Unrelated expansion bundled into a span-consumer PR: reviewers of the flusher change must vet a docs convention change, and reverting or cherry-picking the flusher work drags the doc change along.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff adds a new helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` that linearly scans `self.process_to_shards_map` and calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. Within the shown diff, no code path calls `_create_process_for_shard` (all restarts go through `_ensure_processes_alive()` → `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`), and tests reference `processes`, `process_to_shards_map`, etc., but not this helper. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Metric tag naming drifts: produce/segment_size use `shard` while wait_produce uses `shards` for the same cardinality-heavy shard-list value. Dashboards and alerts built on one tag name miss the other series, and the comma-joined shard-list tag creates unbounded tag combinations that inflate metrics cardinality per process grouping.

[ADVISORY] test_basic now relies on a real `time.sleep(0.1)` to wait for a spawn-mode flusher, introducing wall-clock flakiness while the very next line monkeypatched sleep away earlier in the same test. On slow or loaded CI the 100ms window is not enough for the spawned flusher to observe the drift change and flush, producing an intermittent empty-`messages` failure unrelated to product code.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only the shard-mapping bookkeeping (counts and dict sizes) and never exercises an actual flush through a shared process, so the core behavior — multiple shards flushed correctly by one process — is untested. A regression where a shared process flushes only the first shard in its list (e.g. an off-by-one in the buffer or the `shards` arg plumbing) passes this test while dropping spans for the remaining shards in production.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the new test only asserts bookkeeping/state (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and that `process_to_shards_map` covers 4 shards) and then immediately `step.join()`s without driving any flush/produce behavior across those mapped shards. Given the new multi-shard-per-process plumbing in `SpanFlusher` (e.g., `process_to_shards_map`, per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)`, and passing `shards` into `main()`), a regression where only the first shard in a shared process is actually flushed would not be caught by this test, as the test never validates spans are produced for each shard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _create_process_for_shards constructs fresh SpansBuffer(shards) instances instead of sharing the buffer instance the consumer's write path uses, so the buffer passed into SpanFlusher is now used only for len(buffer.assigned_shards) and every flusher-side buffer is a disconnected empty instance. Any SpansBuffer state that is instance-local rather than derived purely from Redis (segment bookkeeping consumed by record_stored_segments, memory accounting used by get_memory_info) exists separately in the writer's buffer and in each per-process buffer; record_stored_segments() in submit() now runs against instances nothing was ever written into, and a restart replaces the buffer again, silently resetting whatever counters/state it held. If any part of the flush path depends on buffer-instance state rather than a pure Redis read, segments are never flushed or are accounted incorrectly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows SpanFlusher no longer stores/uses the original `buffer` instance (`self.buffer` assignment was removed) and instead constructs new per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances in `_create_process_for_shards`, and `submit()` now calls `record_stored_segments()` / `get_memory_info()` on these newly created buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values()`). This is a concrete design change that could be problematic if `SpansBuffer` maintains any instance-local counters/state (especially across restarts, where a new `SpansBuffer` is created again), but the diff does not include `SpansBuffer`’s implementation, so it cannot be conclusively verified as a functional bug solely from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) makes the factory default (flusher_processes=None) spawn one process per shard, while the new CLI option defaults to 1, so existing non-CLI constructions of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory silently change from 1 flusher process to N processes. Every caller that constructs ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without passing flusher_processes (other consumers, dev tooling, tests) multiprocesses the flusher without opting in, multiplying spawn-process count and Redis polling load by the shard count; additionally a configured flusher_processes=0 silently falls back to one-process-per-shard via the `or` instead of being rejected or clamped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the default behavior when `flusher_processes` is not provided: `SpanFlusher.__init__` sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, and `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` passes `max_processes=self.flusher_processes` where `flusher_processes` defaults to `None`. That means direct (non-CLI) constructions now default to `len(assigned_shards)` processes (effectively one-per-shard via `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/performance change and is inconsistent with the new CLI option default of `1` process. However, the diff’s updated docstring explicitly states it "Creates one process per shard", so this may be intentional rather than a correctness defect. The `flusher_processes=0` point is also true (`0` is falsy and falls back to per-shard), but the diff doesn’t specify that `0` should be rejected, making it more of an edge-case/contract concern than a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The two adjacent timers tag the same value under different tag names: metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag}) vs metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag}). Dashboards and alerts that group by one tag name silently miss the other metric's per-shard breakdown, and the newly tagged segment_size_bytes uses "shard" while wait_produce uses "shards", so per-shard latency comparison across the flush pipeline is impossible without a metric-name fix deploy.
matched_golden_ids: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same inconsistency in metric tag keys ('shard' vs 'shards') for the same shard identifier across SpanFlusher flush-stage metrics, and explains the resulting aggregation/dashboard/alert breakage and inability to compare per-shard stages. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backpressure check now raises MessageRejected if ANY single process's backpressure_since is past the threshold, so one slow/hung shard process backpressures the entire consumer including shards assigned to healthy processes. With flusher_processes > 1, a single lagging shard (e.g., one hot org's segments) stalls ingestion for all partitions, whereas previously backpressure reflected the single shared flusher; operators see consumer-wide throughput drops traceable to one shard, and the multi-process parallelism this PR adds is negated whenever any one process falls behind.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the backpressure logic now iterates over `self.process_backpressure_since.values()` and raises `MessageRejected()` if **any** process’s `backpressure_since` exceeds the threshold (`for backpressure_since in ...: if ...: raise MessageRejected()`). With the new multi-process design (per-process shard groups in `process_to_shards_map` / `process_backpressure_since`), this means one unhealthy/slow shard-group process can cause the whole consumer step to reject messages, rather than isolating backpressure to only the affected shards/process. This is a diff-grounded behavioral/throughput concern introduced by the parallelization change, but it’s not unambiguously a correctness defect from the diff alone (could be an intentional global safety mechanism).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — no call site exists in this diff; restarts route exclusively through _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards). The next reader must determine whether per-shard restart (and its interaction with the process_to_shards_map) is a supported path; the unused method implies an intended restart granularity that was never wired up, and it will silently rot if the mapping shape changes.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly introduced but the diff shows no call sites for it. All restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and initial creation uses `_create_processes` → `_create_process_for_shards`. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` effectively dead code in the shown changes and suggests an unimplemented/unused per-shard restart path that could rot as `process_to_shards_map` evolves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In join(), the `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the entire for-loop over processes, so once the deadline expires no remaining process gets the terminate() call that the old single-process code always executed. On a join timeout, all but the already-processed prefix of flusher processes are abandoned without terminate(); they survive as daemon processes until interpreter exit, and any shutdown path that relies on terminate() to unblock a stuck flusher (e.g., a hung Redis poll in main) now leaves N-1 processes spinning during the rest of shutdown.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` does `if remaining_time <= 0: break`, which exits the entire loop before reaching the remaining processes. Since `process.terminate()` is called inside the loop after waiting, any processes not yet iterated (the suffix) will not receive `terminate()` on timeout. This is a behavioral regression from the previous single-process code path where `terminate()` was always executed, and it can leave additional flusher processes alive during shutdown if they don’t exit promptly after `self.stopped.value = True` (e.g., stuck work).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Unhealthy detection now operates at process granularity but reports and restarts per shared process: a hang caused by one shard's data kills and restarts the process serving all its co-assigned shards, and the unhealthy metric is emitted once per shard with no way to attribute which shard caused it. Operators debugging flusher_unhealthy spikes see every shard in the group flagged simultaneously and cannot distinguish the offending shard; with the default round-robin assignment i % num_processes, a single pathological shard repeatedly crashes its co-tenant shards' flushing, and the shared process_restarts counter trips the consumer-restarting RuntimeError due to one shard's bad data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly groups multiple shards into a single flusher worker via round-robin mapping (`process_index = i % self.num_processes`, `process_to_shards_map`) and then monitors/restarts health at the process level (`process_healthy_since[...]`, `_ensure_processes_alive`). When a process is unhealthy, it emits `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` once for *each shard in that process* (`for shard in shards: metrics.incr(... tags={..., "shard": shard})`) and restarts the single shared worker (`_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`), so operators will see all co-assigned shards flagged together and cannot infer which shard triggered the hang/crash. This is an operational/observability and isolation tradeoff introduced by the new shard-sharing design, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a threaded flusher (produce_to_pipe path) is judged unhealthy with cause 'hang', the code restarts the process without terminating the old one, leaving two flusher threads polling the same shards. The old thread's loop continues until self.stopped is set (only at join), so both the old and new thread flush the same shards and produce duplicate span segment payloads to Kafka; downstream consumers see duplicated data. The old single-process code crashed loudly here (AttributeError on Thread.kill escaping the ValueError-only handler); the new code silently converts that crash into data duplication.

adjudication.rationale: In the threaded flusher path (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`) and stores it in `self.processes`. When `_ensure_processes_alive` detects a hang (`time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[process_index].value > max_unhealthy_seconds`), it restarts via `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` but only attempts to kill the old worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. There is no termination/join/stop mechanism for the old thread beyond the shared `self.stopped` flag, which is only set in `join()`. Therefore, after a 'hang' restart, the old thread can continue polling/producing while the new thread also runs for the same `shards`, causing duplicate flushing/production. This matches the finding and is directly implied by the new restart logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The added 'give flusher threads time to process' time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op lambda two lines earlier. The synchronization step the test author added to fix a race does nothing, so test_basic still races between the flusher thread's polling loop and step.join(); the test remains flaky and the review iteration that 'fixed' the flakiness changed nothing, masking the real synchronization gap.
matched_golden_ids: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The docstring now claims 'Creates one process per shard' while the code implements round-robin shard grouping via process_to_shards_map, and the effective default (max_processes None -> len(buffer.assigned_shards)) diverges from the CLI default of 1. The stated intent in the artifact contradicts the implemented behavior; callers that construct ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without the new flag silently move from one flusher process to one-per-shard spawn processes (N× process count, N× Redis connections), a resource-usage change no human explicitly accepted since the user-facing default was pinned to 1.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.__init__` now sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, creating a `process_to_shards_map` that round-robins shards across processes. This means (a) the docstring claim “Creates one process per shard” is only strictly true when `max_processes` is >= shard count; otherwise shards are grouped per process, and (b) callers that instantiate `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` without specifying `flusher_processes` will pass `None` to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`, which defaults to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and thus can change behavior from the previous single flusher process to one-per-shard. The CLI option added defaults to 1, but that doesn’t prevent non-CLI callers from getting the new higher default. This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior/resource-usage concern, not a proven correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_basic was silently changed from @pytest.mark.django_db to @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True) without explanation, weakening test isolation to make the new multiprocess path pass. The test now runs against a non-transactional database, so any real bug in the multiprocess flush path that manifests as transaction interaction is hidden rather than caught; future failures in this test will be harder to attribute because the isolation change was made to accommodate the implementation rather than reviewed as a behavioral signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `test_basic` from `@pytest.mark.django_db` to `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)`, but the finding’s core claim is incorrect: `transaction=True` in pytest-django enables real database transactions (TransactionTestCase-style) rather than making the test “non-transactional.” The diff also doesn’t show evidence that this change was made to “weaken isolation” or “hide” transaction-interaction bugs; it more plausibly allows transactional behavior needed by the new multi-process/thread flusher changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new metric tags use inconsistent keys: 'shard' on spans.buffer.flusher.produce/segment_size_bytes but 'shards' on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce. Dashboards and alerts that group by shard tag will split wait_produce data into a separate tag dimension, producing silently fragmented metrics for operators monitoring the new per-shard health behavior this PR introduces.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the metrics for `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `{"shard": shard_tag}`, but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `{"shards": shard_tag}`. This inconsistency is directly visible in the diff and would fragment metric grouping/alerting across two different tag keys, but it does not break runtime correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten join() breaks out of the process loop when the deadline expires, skipping terminate() for all remaining processes, and never terminates threaded flushers at all. On shutdown timeout, some spawn processes are left running past the consumer's join deadline (previously the single process was always terminated), leaking spawn processes holding Redis connections during deploy restarts.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the new loop over self.processes breaks entirely when the deadline expires (`if remaining_time <= 0: break`), which skips the subsequent `process.terminate()` for any remaining multiprocessing processes that were not yet iterated. This differs from the previous single-process behavior where the process would always be terminated after the wait loop. As written, on shutdown timeout, some SpawnProcess instances can remain running past the join deadline, potentially leaking resources (e.g., Redis connections). Thread-based flushers are also never force-stopped here (only polled via is_alive), but that was also true previously; the verifiable regression is the skipped terminate for remaining spawn processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The multi-process restart and health-monitoring logic (_ensure_processes_alive, per-process restart counters, shard-group restarts) has no test coverage in this diff. A regression in the restart path — e.g. the duplicate-thread bug or the restart counter now incrementing per poll across a shared shard group — would ship silently, since both new tests only exercise the healthy happy path where no process dies or hangs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial restart/health logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (per-process `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`, killing/recreating a process for a shard group via `_create_process_for_shards`). The added/modified tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and `test_flusher`) only assert normal/healthy behavior (process/shard mapping, backpressure value presence) and do not simulate `process.is_alive() == False` or a hung process (`time.time() - process_healthy_since > max_unhealthy_seconds`) to exercise restart counters and group restarts. So a regression in the restart path could ship without detection, as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] test_basic adds `time.sleep(0.1)` 'to give flusher threads time to process', but the test's first line monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), so the added sleep does nothing and the test still depends on a race between the flusher process and step.join(). The test is flaky in exactly the way the added lines claim to fix: if the flusher hasn't yet drained the segment when step.join()/step.poll() completes, messages is empty and `(msg,) = messages` raises IndexError; on faster machines it passes while never actually synchronizing, giving false confidence in the new multiprocess flush path.
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op and then later calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to delay, so the sleep does nothing and the test remains race/flaky. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only the flusher's internal bookkeeping (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, total_shards) and never submits any message or asserts any flushed payload, so it verifies the constructor's shard-mapping arithmetic, not parallel flushing behavior. A regression in the actual sharding logic — e.g. _create_process_for_shards restarting the wrong process, or a process flushing the wrong shards (the shard->process map is never exercised at runtime) — passes this test; only test_flusher.py's single-process backpressure assertion covers the flusher at all, so the core new behavior (multiple processes each flushing their own shards) has zero behavioral coverage in the diff (checked: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py and test_flusher.py are the only changed spec files).

adjudication.rationale: In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py, the new test_flusher_processes_limit only constructs the ProcessSpansStrategyFactory with flusher_processes=2, calls create_with_partitions, and asserts internal fields on fac._flusher (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, and that process_to_shards_map covers 4 shards) before step.join(). It never submits any messages/ints into the strategy, never waits for or asserts produced KafkaPayloads, and therefore doesn’t exercise runtime shard isolation or per-process flushing behavior introduced in SpanFlusher (_create_process_for_shards, buffers per process, per-process health/backpressure). This is a specific coverage gap for the new multi-process sharding behavior, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The old assertion `flusher.backpressure_since.value` was replaced with `any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`, which passes when any single process is in backpressure even though the new submit() raises MessageRejected only per-process — the test no longer pins which process's backpressure triggered and would pass even if only one of N processes is stuck while the test's submit path depends on all of them. A bug in the new submit() loop (e.g. iterating only the first process's backpressure_since due to a dict mutation during restart) still satisfies this assertion, weakening the backpressure regression guard compared to the pre-diff test.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher.submit()` now iterates over **all** `self.process_backpressure_since.values()` and raises `MessageRejected` if **any** process has been in backpressure longer than the threshold. That is not “per-process only”; it is an any-process global rejection. Therefore updating the test assertion from `flusher.backpressure_since.value` (single value) to `any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())` matches the new multi-process state and does not inherently weaken the regression guard in the way described. The mention of dict mutation causing only the first process to be checked is speculative and not evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reworked _ensure_processes_alive restart path — including the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) kill guard for thread-mode flushers, and _create_process_for_shards — is exercised by no test in the diff (checked: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py only asserts backpressure state; test_consumer.py only asserts process counts and a happy-path flush). A regression in the restart loop — e.g. self.process_restarts[process_index] incremented but _create_process_for_shards never replacing the dead entry, leaving self.processes holding a dead process forever — ships silently; the thread-mode (produce_to_pipe) branch where process.kill() is skipped is entirely untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new restart/health-check logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` (per-process `process_restarts` counters, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError path, conditional `process.kill()` only for `multiprocessing.Process`, and respawn via `_create_process_for_shards`). The only new/modified tests shown are `test_basic` (happy-path flush), `test_flusher_processes_limit` (verifies process count/shard mapping), and `test_flusher` (asserts any backpressure value). None of these exercise an unhealthy/dead flusher (e.g., `is_alive()==False` or `healthy_since` exceeding threshold), the restart counter increment/limit behavior, or the thread-mode branch (`produce_to_pipe` -> `threading.Thread`) where `kill()` is skipped. This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap for newly introduced nontrivial behavior, not a proven functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both tests were converted from @pytest.mark.django_db to @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True) with no comment or associated production change explaining why transactional DB access is now required. Transactional tests are slower and cannot use TestCase-level rollback isolation; if the conversion was needed because the spawn-based flusher processes access the DB outside the test transaction, that cross-process DB dependency is itself untested behavior that will behave differently in production (real spawned processes) than under the test runner.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `test_basic` and the new `test_flusher_processes_limit` are marked `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)` (changed from plain `django_db` in `test_basic`, and explicitly added in the new test) without any explanation in the test itself. This is a concrete, diff-grounded concern because transactional DB tests are typically slower/more permissive than needed, and in these tests the flusher is configured with `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, which makes `SpanFlusher` use the `threading.Thread` path (not a spawned `multiprocessing.Process`), so the rationale about spawn/DB behavior is not evidenced by the diff. The broader claim about cross-process DB dependencies is speculative, but the unexplained switch to transactional DB access is real and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] join()'s `break` on deadline exhaustion skips the terminate() (and any wait) for every remaining process, so on shutdown timeout only the first process is ever terminated. With multiple flusher processes, once the join deadline expires while waiting on the first process, the loop breaks and processes 2..N are never terminated or joined — orphaned spawn processes keep flushing Redis and producing to Kafka after the consumer has been torn down, duplicating work against whatever replacement consumer takes over the partitions. The old single-process code called terminate() unconditionally.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` computes `remaining_time` and executes `break` when the deadline is exhausted **before** reaching the later processes. Because the `terminate()` call is inside the per-process loop, any processes after the one that consumed the timeout are neither waited on nor terminated (e.g., `for process_index, process in self.processes.items(): ... if remaining_time <= 0: break ... while process.is_alive() ...; if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`). This matches the finding: with multiple flusher processes, a timeout while waiting on an earlier process can skip termination of processes 2..N.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] For threading.Thread flushers (produce_to_pipe path), a process diagnosed as 'hang' is never stopped — the isinstance guard skips kill() and a replacement thread is started for the same shards while the hung thread keeps running. Two threads concurrently poll and flush the same Redis shards, racing to produce the same segments to Kafka and fighting over Redis deletes — duplicate payloads and corrupted flush bookkeeping; the 'restarted' process is a lie because the old one is still alive. Anyone running the flusher with produce_to_pipe (tests, in-memory pipelines) gets silent duplicate work after any hang.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, a “hang” is detected when `time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[process_index].value > max_unhealthy_seconds`, and then a restart is performed via `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. However, the attempted termination is guarded by `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`, so when `produce_to_pipe is not None` the flusher uses `threading.Thread` (see `_create_process_for_shards`), and the hung thread is never stopped/terminated before starting a replacement. That can leave two live threads handling the same `shards` concurrently, since the restart reuses the same shard assignment (`process_to_shards_map`) and creates a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` polling the same Redis shards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit flusher_processes of 0 as 'unset', silently escalating it to one-process-per-shard. An operator who passes --flusher-processes 0 (or a config that computes 0) intending to disable parallelism/disable flushing gets the maximum fan-out instead; the falsy-zero makes the CLI default=1 option's semantics undocumented and unenforceable, and any negative value produces num_processes < 0 and zero flusher processes with no error.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will treat an explicitly provided `max_processes=0` as falsy and replace it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, changing operator intent and potentially causing maximum fan-out. Additionally, negative `max_processes` is accepted (CLI uses `type=int` with no bounds), leading to `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becoming negative; this makes `range(self.num_processes)` empty and then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` in the shard distribution loop can raise (and/or map access fails), i.e., broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — nothing in the diff or its call sites invokes it. Future maintainers get a misleadingly-named single-shard restart helper that silently restarts the whole shared process (it delegates to _create_process_for_shards), so a caller using it to restart one shard actually kills and recreates the process owning several shards, momentarily stopping flushes for unrelated shards.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard` is newly added (in `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`) but there is no invocation of it anywhere in the shown changes; the live path uses `_create_processes()`, `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, and `_ensure_processes_alive()`. So within this diff it is effectively dead/unused code. The advisory about the name being misleading is also grounded: `_create_process_for_shard` just finds the owning `process_index` and delegates to `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, which restarts the process for the whole shard group, not an individual shard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Metric tag key drifts between 'shard' (produce timer, segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (wait_produce timer) for the same comma-joined shard list. Dashboards/alerts that group by shard tag silently miss the wait_produce series (or vice versa), so a hang in the produce-wait stage looks like a gap rather than a slow stage; also the comma-joined multi-shard tag value creates a distinct series per shard-grouping permutation, fragmenting the metric.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the same comma-joined shard list (`shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))`) is emitted under different metric tag keys: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This diff-grounded inconsistency will split series/dashboards by tag key and can hide correlations. Also, using a comma-joined multi-shard value as a tag will create distinct series per shard-group combination, fragmenting metrics.
